raised.claim: The body exclusion only recognizes `.test.ts` files and the two named test roots, so other conventional TypeScript test layouts such as `src/foo.spec.ts` or `src/__tests__/foo.ts` still consume the context budget.
raised.why_it_breaks: If a PR changes a large `src/foo.spec.ts` alongside production source, `filterReviewableFiles` admits it through `src/**/*.ts` but `contextReader` does not exclude it, allowing its body to displace source files despite the new behavior being intended to withhold test bodies.

raised.claim: The new argument parser silently ignores all positional arguments after the optional base SHA instead of rejecting an invalid invocation.
raised.why_it_breaks: For an invocation such as `418 abc123 deadbee`, whether `deadbee` was intended as a corrected base or as the historical head, it is discarded and replay runs `abc123..current-head`, producing measurements for a different commit range without warning.

raised.claim: A historical `--head` replay still sends the PR's current title and body to the finder, so it does not faithfully reconstruct the prompt seen at that head.
raised.why_it_breaks: If the PR description is edited after the requested historical commit—for example to document fixes or remove original requirements—`--head <old-sha>` reads files from the old SHA but supplies the updated description, causing recall/model comparisons to measure a prompt that the live review never saw.

raised.claim: The historical-head fallback assumes the base repository's Git server permits fetching an unreachable commit by raw SHA, which is not guaranteed for a force-pushed PR commit.
raised.why_it_breaks: For an old commit removed by a force-push, `pull/<pr>/head` only supplies the current head; if the old object is no longer advertised or raw object wants are denied by the server, `git fetch origin <sha>` fails and the new `--head` recall replay exits even though this is the exact state the option is intended to handle.
